760230101.text: I can't imagine how you two warriors managed to make it through the thunderstorm, but... that's not the point right now. I need your help!

760230102.text: Don't worry, there's no way we'd stand by while someone needs help. What do you need us to do?

760230103.text: Please, help me get the <color=#00E1FFFF>Airspace Data Collector</color> up in the air!

760230104.text: Airspace Data Collector...? You mean that big round machine?

760230105.text: That's right! All you need to do is <color=#00E1FFFF>align the strong kuuvahki side of each assembly module with the collector, and push them into place</color>.

760230106.text: Then the collector — ah, I mean that big round machine — will float up into the air. That means everything's working!

760230107.text: #Alright, seeing how desperate you are... Let's help him out, {NICKNAME}.

760230108.text: Thank you so much! I really appreciate it!

760230201.text: Please, don't strike me... I still have work to do!

760232401.text: Good news! I've made a breakthrough!

760232402.text: I'm 99.5% sure that the Fanngel Effect didn't affect either of you.

760232403.text: That's great, though Paimon wasn't really concerned about that... But if it wasn't because of the Fanngel Effect, then why did the collector get struck last time?

760232404.text: Because the lightning protection device inside the collector was never tested for repeated use in such a high kuuvahki environment. The materials eventually gave out from fatigue.

760232405.text: The fix was actually pretty simple. I tested a bunch of materials with different parameters based on this area's kuuvahki concentration, and found something way more durable. Look—

760232406.text: This is the <color=#00E1FFFF>Nod-Krai Airspace Data Collector 2.0</color> — I stayed up all night to finish it. With one final high-altitude test, we'll be able to determine the experiment's results!

760232407.text: Why is the Collector 2.0 so much smaller than the previous one?

760232408.text: Advanced models are usually more compact.

760232409.text: #Oh, Paimon gets it now! So, Paimon really is more advanced than {NICKNAME}!

760232410.text: Hehe... While that's usually true, the reason the 2.0 model shrank so much this time was actually due to the limits of the materials used. I had to cut a lot of non-essential features—

760232411.text: For example, the entire structure for lifting it into the air...

760232412.text: Huh? If it can't get up in the air, how is it supposed to collect data from high altitudes?

760232413.text: Uhm... Well... Ah — It's all because... You see... Many of the greatest leaps in human knowledge come when the researchers themselves step in. Even if it means becoming the subject of their own experiments.

760232414.text: They say Heinry's team drank tens of thousands of bottles of Fonta to perfect the flavor we have today. So... You get what I'm saying, right?

760232416.text: Staring at us won't make us understand, you know.

760232417.text: *sigh* You are way too smart not to get this. But fine, if you insist...

760232421.text: #How about this — I'll just redesign the Fannta bottle to be shaped like you two... or we don't even have to call it Fannta anymore. It could be Paita, Monta, or {NICKNAME}-ta.

760232422.text: Please, for the sake of scientific progress, take the Collector 2.0 with you into the skies!

760232419.text: Huh!? Not me! It's enough of a miracle that the Fanngel Effect hasn't affected you two. If I were the one to try it, it'd be a total disaster...

760232420.text: Not that I'd mind trying. Sooner or later, the curse will devour me anyway. But the research on kuuvahki is too important to be left unfinished...

subQuests.subQuestName: Push each assembly module to the correct orientation and position

760230402.text: Oh, right! I just noticed that <color=#00E1FFFF>there's a signal issue in one of the three channels, but it can be fixed by resetting the robot</color>. Now, let me set up the experimental parameters!

760230403.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

760230501.text: Sure, just give me a moment.

760230502.text: Alright. I'll inspect the collector's hardware in the meantime.

760231002.text: Oh, right! I just noticed that <color=#00E1FFFF>there's a signal issue in one of the three channels, but it can be fixed by resetting the robot</color>. Now, let me set up the experimental parameters!

760231003.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

subQuests.subQuestName: Push each assembly module to the correct orientation and position

760232501.text: The experiment was a success! Just as I thought, kuuvahki has huge potential!

760232502.text: Thank you both. This is the critical data I was missing. Once I've combed through it all, I can finally get started on my thesis.

760232503.text: I hope the research results on kuuvahki will truly achieve what Mr. Raimondo envisioned — freeing people from their reliance on Arkhium. This would be an enormous step forward.

760232504.text: Looks like we actually helped with something big. That's awesome!

760232505.text: Indeed, progress marches forward! My thesis should be done in a year or two. And maybe in twenty or thirty more, we'll start to see the real impact of what we did today.

760232506.text: T—Twenty or t—thirty years?! That long?

760232507.text: That sort of time frame is already a breakneck breakthrough! Scientific research takes time, you know. It's all about patience and precision. We can't rush it...

760232508.text: #Alright, fine... Paimon really thought we'd get to try a bottle of Fann-{NICKNAME}-Paimon-ta any day now...

760232509.text: I'll be sure to suggest that to Heinry and the team! Oh, and here, take the Nod-Krai Airspace Data Collector 2.0 as thanks from me.

760232510.text: I've removed the data collection module, since it's classified tech from the Institute. I hope you understand.

760232511.text: It no longer has any data collection functionality, but the lightning protection still works. Hopefully, it'll come in handy on your adventures.

760232512.text: Just a heads-up! It only works on thunderstorms that carry kuuvahki. It won't be effective against regular lightning, so once you're outside Nod-Krai, it probably won't be of much use...

760232513.text: Wow! That means we don't have to worry about getting struck by lightning while we're out exploring!

760232514.text: Science really can defeat a curse!

760232515.text: Haha, well said! And finally, thank you both again for your contribution to science. Once I've sorted through the raw data, it's time for me to head back to the Institute and start writing my thesis.

760232902.text: We'll need higher-altitude data this time, so <color=#00E1FFFF>we'll need to stack three assembly modules for each channel</color>. However, you only need to manually adjust the modules for two of the channels. Leave the rest to me.

760232903.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

760231802.text: We'll need higher-altitude data this time, so <color=#00E1FFFF>we'll need to stack three assembly modules for each channel</color>. However, you only need to manually adjust the modules for two of the channels. Leave the rest to me.

760231803.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

subQuests.subQuestName: Push each assembly module to the designated position

760231101.text: Sure, just give me a moment.

760231102.text: Alright. I'll inspect the collector's hardware in the meantime.

760232201.text: Fanngel! Th—There was an accident... The collector got hit by lightning...

760232202.text: Yes, I saw it too. The Fanngel Effect... It's intensified. Even with the lightning protection device and your help, we can't hold it back...

760232203.text: W—Well, things might not be that bad. Don't give up just yet...

760232204.text: The only way to break the curse is by advancing science.

760232205.text: Exactly. According to your theory, the only one who can defeat the Fanngel Effect now is you, Fanngel!

760232206.text: Oh! You're right. If I fail, this curse won't just destroy me. It will destroy everything I hold dear.

760232207.text: If, in the end, even the Fontaine Research Institute is... is... I would never forgive myself.

760232208.text: We're at a critical stage of the experiment. Based on my initial analysis, kuuvahki does indeed seem safer than Arkhium.

760232209.text: But for real-world applications, that conductive phenomenon we just observed must never be allowed to happen. I have to identify the cause.

760232210.text: The collector's crashed... It's certainly unfortunate, but what really matters is the data inside. Could I ask you to retrieve it for me?

760232212.text: Please be careful! I'll check here to see if the issue was caused by the equipment itself.

subQuests.subQuestName: Find the crashed collector and recover the experiment data
Bring the experiment data to Fanngel

760232301.text: I was starting to worry the Fanngel Effect might've gotten to you, too... So, how did it go? Did you get the data?

760232302.text: We got it, but the collector was already...

760232303.text: I suspected as much... The designs never accounted for the impact from a fall. *sigh* That was my oversight.

760232304.text: I've found a few leads on my end as well, but it's too early to draw any conclusions. I'll need to analyze them together with the data you recovered.

760232305.text: Give me some time to dig into it. Could you come by again tomorrow?

760231601.text: We've got the data! So that means we're done here, right?

760231602.text: I'm sorry, but we still need data from higher altitudes... That's how scientific research works. It's all about patience and precision. We can't rush it.

760231603.text: Okay, but... you didn't get struck by lightning when you went to set the parameters just now, did you? Maybe that curse of yours isn't as bad as you think! So for this next experiment...

760231604.text: No, no! It has to be the two of you conducting the experiment. If I tried, something would definitely go wrong. Please, you have to believe me!

760231606.text: Paimon suddenly feels like renaming Fonta might not be enough...

760231607.text: No problem! As long as you're willing to keep helping with the experiment, then putting your likenesses on the Fannta label would be more than fair!

760231608.text: #So that means everyone who buys Fannta will get to see Paimon and {NICKNAME} on the label?

760231609.text: Yes! You'll be known around Teyvat. But for two scientific pioneers like yourselves, that's still a pretty modest reward. So, what do you say? Shall we keep going?

760231611.text: I've known Heinry for years. I'm sure he'll agree if I say the right words. If not... well, we can always add his name to the label too!

760231612.text: After all, what we seek has never been glory, but scientific progress itself.

760231614.text: In that case, let's get back to the experiment!

760231615.text: Excellent! I knew you were people of extraordinary insight. Once you're ready, I'll go set up the parameters for the next experiment.

760231701.text: Are you ready? Shall we move on to the next experiment?

760231902.text: Alright, no problem. I could use some time to analyze the data you gathered earlier.

760230901.text: Are you ready to begin the next experiment?

760231301.text: F—Finally, it worked! Warriors, my name is Fanngel. I'm a researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute.

760231302.text: I saw everything just now. You were absolutely incredible! May I ask your names?

760231303.text: #Paimon's Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers. Have you been stuck here for a long time?

760231304.text: If not for the two of you, I might've been stuck much longer... You're the first ones to make it through the thunderstorm safely!

760231306.text: N—No, of course not! I... don't have your luck.

760231308.text: You probably won't believe me... but this abnormal weather is probably a result of my being cursed...

760231309.text: Cursed? Wait, do sciencey people really believe in that kind of thing?

760231310.text: Indeed. In fact, that's why I got into science in the first place — to find a way to break this curse. I know it sounds crazy, but if you'd gone through half the things I have, you'd understand.

760231311.text: Whenever I cook, even when I'm just mixing a salad, it somehow catches fire. If I hang out the laundry, a tornado is guaranteed to blow it away... Things like that happen to me every — single — day. I call it the "Fanngel Effect."

760231312.text: That really does sound unlucky... Isn't there a way to break the curse?

760231313.text: Science, of course! That's the only way!

760231314.text: That sounds reasonable enough, but something feels off...

760232001.text: Wonderful! With your help, I no longer have to worry about the Fanngel Effect messing up the experiment!

760232601.text: Hmm... Data sorting is a meticulous task. I'll have to remain fully focused...

760232603.text: Once my thesis is finished and published, I'll make sure to send you a copy. Well then, time for me to get back to my research...

760232605.text: Our understanding of kuuvahki is still quite limited. I'm considering spending more time in Nod-Krai to conduct further field research.

760232607.text: It's pretty effective, right? I take my research seriously, after all.

760232609.text: You too! Best of luck with your adventures!

760232701.text: F—Finally, it worked! Warriors, my name is Fanngel. I'm a researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute.

760232702.text: I saw everything just now. You were absolutely incredible! May I ask your names?

760232712.text: That really does sound unlucky... Isn't there a way to break the curse?

760232713.text: Science, of course! That's the only way!

760232714.text: That sounds reasonable enough, but something feels off...

760233002.text: Alright, no problem. I could use some time to analyze the data you gathered earlier.

760233601.text: This will be the final experiment. <color=#00E1FFFF>Channel the lightning to the lightning rod over there, then launch up and collect the data.</color> The lightning protection device in the Collector 2.0 will keep you safe.

760233602.text: I'll let you know as soon as we've got enough data. And I'll do everything I can to keep you safe. So, ready to go?

760233801.text: I still need a little more time...

760233802.text: That's fine — the more thorough the preparations, the smoother the experiment tends to go. Just come find me when you're ready!

760233901.text: The experiment parameters are all set. I'm counting on you to launch the collector.

760234401.text: Looks like the collector's beyond repair. That means these assembly modules are useless, too. *sigh* I've worked on this for so long...

760234402.text: The Fanngel Effect has definitely intensified... but this isn't the time to worry about that. I'll focus on checking the equipment first.

760234701.text: Apart from the materials, could something else be going wrong?

760235001.text: See that lightning rod over there? I set it up specially for this experiment. It can convert kuuvahki into an upward force field.

760235002.text: I've already run the tests, and in theory it should work. Now it's up to you to put it into practice!
